oneLiner: The sole enabler of leading-edge AI silicon: every major accelerator is fabbed here, N2 is sold out through 2026, and the old geopolitical discount has largely compressed out of the multiple.
thesis: Effective monopoly at 2nm-class: N2 entered high-volume manufacturing Dec 2025, fully allocated through 2026, targeting ~100K wafers/month by year-end; Intel 18A yields lag to 2027 and Samsung SF2 struggles with GAA.
HPC (the AI complex: NVDA, AMD, Broadcom ASICs, Apple compute) is now 66% of revenue and growing 20% QoQ.
2026 revenue growth guided to slightly above 40% YoY in USD with 65-67% gross margins despite overseas-fab dilution.
Advanced packaging (CoWoS) is a second bottleneck TSMC controls; customer PDK/IP ecosystems make leading-edge defection a multi-year, high-risk project.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun; reported Jul 16, 2026)
points: Revenue $40.2B, +36% YoY, +12% QoQ, high end of guidance.
Gross margin 67.7% (above guide); operating margin 60.3%; ADR EPS $4.31, +77% YoY.
Guide: Q3 revenue $44.6-45.8B, gross margin 65-67%; FY2026 growth raised to slightly above 40%.
Node mix: N5 33%, N3 30%, N7 11%, N2 3% (first material quarter); 7nm-and-below = 77% of wafer revenue.
Platform mix: HPC 66%, Smartphone 22% (-4% QoQ), IoT 5%, Automotive 4%.

segments: HPC 66% of revenue: AI accelerators, custom ASICs, Apple silicon compute.
Smartphone 22%: fall 2026 iPhone silicon on N2 is the next leg.
competitive: Intel 18A reached HVM late 2025 but Intel concedes world-class yields only by 2027, limiting external foundry wins.
Samsung SF2 prioritizing GAA yield recovery over leapfrogging.
Reported N2 pricing ~$30K/wafer with capacity booked to 2028 (trade press, unverified).
Practically every leading AI accelerator (NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Trainium, Cerebras) is fabbed at TSMC.
moat: Process leadership plus yield/scale economics, advanced-packaging control, and a customer ecosystem (PDKs, IP, design services) that makes defection a multi-year project. N2 sold out through 2026 before it ramped.
risks: Geopolitics: leading-edge concentration in Taiwan remains the structural discount driver.
AI capex cyclicality: at 66% HPC, a hyperscaler digestion year hits far harder than prior cycles.
Customer concentration: Apple historically ~25% of revenue, NVIDIA rising fast.
Margin dilution: record $52-56B capex including Arizona, Japan, Dresden; management guides gross margin down to 65-67%.
Currency: NTD appreciation compresses reported margins (USD revenue, NTD costs).
Smartphone softness: 22% of revenue declined 4% QoQ.
catalysts: N2 ramp to ~100K wpm by end-2026; N2P/A16 progression in 2027.
2027 capex framing on the October call.
NVIDIA Rubin volume ramp (Q4 2026) flows through TSMC N3/N2 and packaging.
pricedIn: Trailing ~35x and forward ~24-26x are well above TSM's own decade norm (mid-teens to 20x forward): the Taiwan discount has largely compressed out after the stock roughly doubled in a year. The multiple embeds 40%+ 2026 growth plus a decent 2027. Debate: are 60%+ operating margins peak-cycle artifacts, and does an AI capex pause turn a structural re-rating back into a cyclical one? The 5% fall after a record Q2 shows expectations are full.

scenarios.bear: Hyperscaler capex digests in 2027 just as record capacity lands; HPC growth stalls; overseas costs and NTD strength pull gross margin to high-50s; multiple mean-reverts toward ~18x forward on renewed geopolitical pricing.
scenarios.base: 2026 closes at 40%+ growth as guided; N2 ramps to ~100K wpm at premium pricing; 2027 slower but healthy; gross margin holds mid-60s; stock tracks earnings at low-to-mid-20s forward.
scenarios.bull: N2 pricing power plus a monopoly-like leading edge while rivals slip; accelerator unit growth compounds through Rubin/MI400/custom ASIC ramps all fabbed here; margins hold at records and the market pays a sustained premium for the sole enabler of the AI build-out.

valPresets.note: Valuation basis is forward earnings, not FCF: TTM FCF is structurally depressed by the record $52-56B capex program, which would make an FCF-DCF read absurdly demanding.

notes: Statement history shown is 4 years (Yahoo) because TSMC files 20-F/6-K rather than 10-K/10-Q; figures converted from TWD at spot. FCF here is capex-heavy: valuation lab base case uses normalized growth off a depressed FCF base.
